correctness.rationale: For every positive real shape the quantile derivative identity is exact; the strictly increasing positive integral kernel g makes the derivative strictly shrink as the shape rises. Integration proves all interior quantile spacings. Strict monotonicity of the centered quantile difference and its zero full integral give strict integrated-quantile dominance and thus strict centered convex order. Finite checker tests independently confirm many quantile and derivative cases, without being used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Literature-led strict quantile-spacing and centered convex ordering for all positive real shapes is not entailed by the published variance monotonicity, nor by the inspected 2021 sufficient condition requiring log-convexity that fails for this law. Related current-indexed scientific abstracts concern different observables. Full text of Giam 2026 and Alimohammadi et al. 2021 remained inaccessible, so historical-priority risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Uninspected full text of Giam (2026) could contain a stronger quantile statement even though its abstract states variance monotonicity only.
Uninspected full text of Alimohammadi–Esna-Ashari–Cramer (2021) or Das–Kayal–Choudhuri (2019) could contain a specialization not apparent in the abstracts.
An unindexed or differently named general dispersive-order theorem may imply the specific result; literature search is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The stochastic order strengthens the specific classical multi-player coupon-collector variance coefficient comparison from a single scalar into every quantile interval and every centered convex risk, while covering a natural real-parameter interpolation. This is a meaningful structural uncertainty ordering motivated by the published conjecture and the literature on extreme-order-statistic dispersion, not a table recomputation.
